questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culture, highly respected university, the weather and nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Arrival was generally smooth. Due to our local advisor from USYD being overworked, replies and e-mails and information could be delayed, but it was not really a problem.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome week at the university, where us exchange students had some special additions to our programme, such as information meetings etc., which was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed at the university-provided Queen Mary Building. Was difficult to get a spot, but I was lucky. Was definately the cheapest option availiable, but still 7000DKK for a single room with shared bathrooms and kitchen. Good facilities. Otherwise Scape is very popular and has several locations thorughout Sydney.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Queen Mary Building was less than 5 mins walk from campus, so that was great. If staying off campus, make sure to check transport connections etc., to make sure it is easy to get to campus and around town.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to fill out several online forms and provide documentation. The proces was slightly confusing and seemed to come close to arrival, but it was not problem. Don't stress about it. However, the proces for registering for classes was chaotic, see below.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a dedicated exchange advisor/coordinator at USYD, why kept us updated and could anwer questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We received a list of units we could take as exchange students. Be aware that these differ significantly from what is listed on the USYD website. There were still many units to choose from, and they let us choose undergraduate courses (make sure to get approved by KU though). Local students get priority, so I did not get a single unit from my initial wishes. There was a second 'round' and I finally got some units. It was stressful, but one can also change/add units within the first 1-2 weeks of classes starting, so there was no need to stress that much. Was unfortunate not being able to get the units I wanted though. Also, some units get extra spaces near the start of the semester, so make sure to watch for that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to respond quickly to e-mails etc. When you receive a task, be sure to complete it as quickly as possible as most things are first come first serve. Be patient with your USYD advisor (long response times) and keep an open mind for units, as you may not get your favorite. Also remember that places on units may open up nearer to the semester, so keep cool.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My impression was that units which are obligatory for local students (e.g. Torts and Contracts etc.) have a very very high workload. Electives have a more reasonable workload and I would not say they are more difficult that at KU. Just different. Also be sure to check which type of exam each unit have, as they are very different and some are by pen and paper. In the electives it was not that difficult to pass, but getting the highest scores is very difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more interactive teaching. All my courses were seminar-based so about 20-40 students. It is expected to have read the materials beforehand and that one engages actively in discussions in class. All teachers are professors so they are very knowledgable and passionate, which was very nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Media Law: Contempt and Open Justice. War Law: The use of force and humanitarian law. The People in constitutional Thought. Philisophy of Criminal Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Media Law was very interesting and I would reccomend it to a real feel and experience of how the common law works in Australia and the UK. Almost all cyllabus is case-law. Is challenging to get used to, as they are written in a very different way than in Denmark. 

War Law was very interesting and more similar to courses in DK. Philisophy of Criminal Law is very theoretial and philisophical, so I reccomend that if that's your thing.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The Student Visa is very expensive (8500dkk).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Generally, prices in Sydney are similar to those in DK. Eating out and takeaway and cafés are a bit cheaper, but otherwise about the same cost of living. Housing is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many sports clubs and other societies. However, some are expensive.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Deffinately go to all the events in the Welcome Week and first weeks of the semester. This is where you will meet most of your new friends. Also prioritise to attend social activities in your accomidation.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Sydney! It is a beautiful city. Also, do the weekend surf camp. You will have about a week of easter holidays, so use that to travel to the east coast or another longer trip. Melbourne and the outback are also must visits.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Australian culture is similar to European culture generally. A bit more American probably. People are very outgoing and social, and having small talk with strangers is common.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A large portion of USYD students are international, with most being from Asia. Some of those stick together and don't really speak with anyone except others from their country. However, I did not really notice this with law students, it was more prevalent in scientific faculties.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Aussies are very relaxed and outgoing and polite, but stuff still just works and is well organised. I found that a very nice combination.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prioritise finding housing and living with outher students from other countries. Attend the welcome week and other events. Explore and enjoy Australia's wonderful cities and nature!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Forming new friendships and adjusting and enjoying a different country and a university which feels very different that KU (mostly in good ways!)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for the heat and very intense sun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
